title: llm-learning-scratchpad-samir-patel-2025
content:
Quick brain dump — mostly for myself. Rough, fragmented. Use this as a living scratchpad for papers/blogs/talks I want to turn into experiments or short writeups.

Top-level themes I'm tracking:
- RAG / retrieval latency vs freshness tradeoffs
- KV-cache management for long-running chats (eviction, sharding, prioritized caching)
- Aggressive quantization (3/4-bit) + per-channel scaling in practice
- Streaming prefetch + decoding overlap on multi-GPU hosts
- Prompt recipes and eval sets for regression detection

Notes from readings (short summaries + one-line takeaways):

1) "Adaptive KV cache for autoregressive transformers" (paper notes) — arXiv 2407.01234
- Idea: Cache entries have a score combining recency, token novelty, and a small learned priority trained with RL to trade latency vs cache hit quality.
- Implementation detail: store compressed KV with 8-bit quantized tensors and a tiny Bloom-filter-ish fingerprint to check probable hit.
- Takeaway: Smart eviction beats naive LRU when conversation patterns have topic-switch bursts. Worth trying a cheap learned priority feature (sigmoid of features) in our runtime.
- Quick experiment idea: simulate on RedTest logs (chat sessions) with synthetic topic shifts; compare LRU vs timed decay vs learned-priority on end-to-end latency and n-gram match.

2) "3-bit quantization with mixed per-channel scaling" (blog + open-sourced kernels)
- Claims: With per-channel scaling and a tiny extra codebook per-channel, 3-bit math gets surprisingly close to 8-bit in many decoder-only models.
- Caveat: Some attention heads remain fragile — need head-wise calibration and optionally keep those heads in 8-bit.
- Implementation note: pipeline-level support required (memory layout, fused matmul + dequant).
- Takeaway: For Dedicated/private deployments this could cut VRAM by ~30-40% but needs kernel support and thorough eval on hallucination/accuracy.

3) Retrieval freshness tradeoffs (notes from an Ops talk at a recent conference)
- Multi-layer cache: local host TTL (ms-level), regional cache (s) and corpus-level reindexing (hours).
- When to prefer re-ranking vs expanding retrieval candidates: re-ranking helps precision but increases latency; expansion helps recall and can be batched.
- Quick idea: expose two endpoints to app developers — "fresh" (always requery) and "fast" (local cache first) and measure product metrics.

4) NeurIPS/ICLR talk highlights (hand-scribbled)
- "Prefetching hidden states for streaming decode": overlap attention KV fetch with next-token score computation, reduces tail latency on long sequences.
- "Model fallback policies" — orchestration that dynamically swaps to smaller quantized variants based on 95th percentile latency window. This is similar to Redwood's routing concept but different heuristics.

Prompt/experiment recipes (very rough)
- Regression probe set: 500 prompts split by length (short/medium/long), by semantic difficulty, and by hallucination-likelihood. Track BLEU-ish and factuality score (automated checks where possible).
- Quantization A/B: run same 50 prompts through FP16 baseline, 4-bit, and 3-bit mixed; measure token-level divergence, lead-time to hallucination, sample-specific stubbornness.
- KV cache experiment: build synthetic store where conversation jumps topics at t=20, t=80; test LRU vs TTL vs learned-priority. Metric: token compute saved vs extra perplexity / hallucination incidents.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- How do we calibrate per-head sensitivity to quantization cheaply? Can we find a proxy metric during offline profiling?
- If we introduce a learned-priority for KV caching, what's the simplest on-device model (logistic regression?) that is cheap to compute per insert evict decision?
- Safety: how does quantization interact with safety filters that run on logits vs sampling output? Need to re-run safety checks end-to-end.

Action items (short-term)
- [ ] Grab a 1k convo sample from RedTest and run offline LRU vs TTL simulation (Samir) — target: 1 week.
- [ ] Prototype per-channel 3-bit dequantization pipeline with smaller model (Red-2B) and run quality checks (collab: Maya) — target: 2 weeks.
- [ ] Draft a short internal note summarizing prefetching talk and propose a micro-benchmark for streaming overlap (collab: Lena) — target: 10 days.

Random prompts and snippets I want to keep here:
- "You are a careful assistant. Always cite the sentence in the retrieved document that supports your answer, if any. If none, say 'no retrieval evidence'."
- Short prompt for eval: "Summarize the document in 2–3 sentences focusing only on factual claims and avoid inference."

Misc links I found while reading:
- Retrieval paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01234
- Quantization cheatsheet (blog): https://blog.efficient-inference.example/quantization-cheatsheet
- Old OpenReview discussion about head-wise sensitivity: https://openreview.net/forum?id=xxxx

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally messy. When something matures, move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime or product/optimize. For now, nightly brain-dump here.

End of session 2025-10-02.
